chunks: Indeed, when the servant prostrates and says, 'O Lord, O Lord,' until his breath is cut off, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says to him, 'Here I am; what is your need?'

key_terms.الرَّبُّ: the Lord, the One who nurtures, sustains, and responds
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the servant of Allah, in a state of humility and devotion
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted is He, an expression of Allah's transcendence and majesty
key_terms.حَاجَتُكَ: your need or request being presented before Allah
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Here I am in response to you; a reply of acceptance
key_terms.نَفَسُهُ: his breath, indicating persistence and intensity in invocation
key_terms.يَا رَبِّ: O my Lord, a direct call of supplication and need

ai.seo_question: What happens when a servant repeatedly calls 'Yā Rabb' while in sajdah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the nearness of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, to a servant who persists in calling upon Him while in sajdah. It highlights the spiritual excellence of repeated du'a in prostration and the servant's humble turning to his Lord.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.976 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"When a servant prostrates and says, 'O’ Lord (azj), O’ Lord (azj),' until their breath runs out, the Lord (azj), Blessed and Exalted, responds,
'Here I am; what is your need?'".
